simple.meaning: רָצַץ (râtsats) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “to crack in pieces, literally or figuratively.” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 19 times across Genesis, Deuteronomy, Judges, 1 Samuel, 2 Kings, and 8 more, beginning at Genesis 25:22. Its contexts include land, Israel.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to רָצַץ (H7533).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.
simple.summary: רָצַץ (râtsats) / H7533 is traced through Genesis 25:22, Deuteronomy 28:33, Judges 9:53, Judges 10:8 as a generated source-based concept entry.

structuredEvidence.definition: to crack in pieces, literally or figuratively

firstOccurrence.englishText: The children struggled together within her. She said, “If it is like this, why do I live?” She went to inquire of Yahweh.

timeline.evidenceText: The children struggled together within her. She said, “If it is like this, why do I live?” She went to inquire of Yahweh.
A nation which you don’t know will eat the fruit of your ground and all of your work. You will only be oppressed and crushed always,
A certain woman cast an upper millstone on Abimelech’s head, and broke his skull.
They troubled and oppressed the children of Israel that year. For eighteen years they oppressed all the children of Israel that were beyond the Jordan in the land of the Amorites, which is in Gilead.

Here I am. Witness against me before Yahweh, and before his anointed. Whose ox have I taken? Whose donkey have I taken? Whom have I defrauded? Whom have I oppressed? Of whose hand have I taken a bribe to make me blind my eyes? I will restore it to you.”
They said, “You have not defrauded us, nor oppressed us, neither have you taken anything from anyone’s hand.”
Now, behold, you trust in the staff of this bruised reed, even in Egypt. If a man leans on it, it will go into his hand, and pierce it. So is Pharaoh king of Egypt to all who trust on him.
Then Asa was angry with the seer, and put him in the prison; for he was in a rage with him because of this thing. Asa oppressed some of the people at the same time.
For he has oppressed and forsaken the poor.
You broke the heads of Leviathan in pieces.

Behold, you trust in the staff of this bruised reed, even in Egypt, which if a man leans on it, it will go into his hand and pierce it. So is Pharaoh king of Egypt to all who trust in him.
He won’t break a bruised reed.
He will not fail nor be discouraged,
“Isn’t this the fast that I have chosen:
When they took hold of you by your hand, you broke, and tore all their shoulders. When they leaned on you, you broke, and paralyzed all of their thighs.”
Listen to this word, you cows of Bashan, who are on the mountain of Samaria, who oppress the poor, who crush the needy, who tell their husbands, “Bring us drinks!”

definitions.short: to crack in pieces, literally or figuratively
definitions.usage: break, bruise, crush, discourage, oppress, struggle together.
definitions.full: H7533. ratsats [ רָצַץ ] verb crush (Late Hebrew = Biblical Hebrew; Arabic bruise, bray, crush ; Aramaic רְעַ , crush, shatter ); — Qal Perfect 2masculine singular suffix רַצּוֺתָנוּ 1Sam 12:4 ; 1 singular רַצּוֺתִי 12:3 ; Imperfect 3masculine singular יָּרוּץ (Ges § 67q ) Isa 42:4 (Babylonian Manuscript יֵרוֺץ , Niph`al, so SS here and Eccl 12:6 a), 3feminine singular תָּרוּץ 12:6 a, 1singular אָרֻץ Psa 18:30 = אָרוּץ 2Sam 22:30 (see below); Participle active feminine plural רֹצְצוֺת Amos 4:1 ; passive רָצוּץ Isa 42:3 +, construct רְצוּץ Hosea 5:11 ; plural רְצוּצִים Isa 58:6 ; — crush: 1 literal, a. passive participle in (הָ)רָצוּץ (הַ)קָּנֶה 2Kin 18:21 = Isa 36:6 ; 42:3 (all metaphor of weak person). b. imperfect intransitive get crushed (read תֵּרוֺץ ?), of bowl Eccl 12:6 a (in metaphor). 2 figurative crush, oppress , accusative of person 1Sam 12:3-4 , Amos 4:1 ; passive participle Deut 28:33 , as substantive the oppressed Isa 58:6 ; מִשְׁמָּט רְצוּץ Hosea 5:11 (We Now רֹצֵץ , i.e. perverting judgment , but dubious); intransitive get crushed (read יֵרוֺץ ?), of servant of ׳י , under figure of wick, Isa 42:4 (+ יִכְהֶה ) he shall not grow dim or be crushed out. Niph`al be crushed, broken: Perfect 3masculine singular consecutive נְרֹץ (Ges § 67t ) Eccl 12:6 b (of wheel at cistern); Imperfect 2masculine singular תֵּרוֺץ Ezek 29:7 (of Pharaoh as reed, compare Qal 1 a ); Job 20:10 read perhaps יֵרֹצּוּ (for יְרַצּוּ , see רצה Pi`el), are crushed (as) poor men, Bu, compare Hoffm SS Gerber. — Isa 42:2 ; Eccl 12:6 a see Qal. Pi`el crush in pieces: 1 literal (in metaphor) Perfect 2masculine singular רִצַּצְתָּ Psa 74:14 with accusative of thing. 2 figurative = grievously oppress , 3 masculine singular רִצַּץ Job 20:19 ; Imperfect 3masculine singular הָעָם מִן וַיְרַצֵּץ 2Chr 16:10 . Po`el Imperfect 3masculine plural וַיְרֹצְצוּ Judg 10:8 , accusative of person (= Pi`el 2 ; || רעץ ; רצץ here perhaps doublet, so GFM Hpt , compare Bu Now). Hiph`il Imperfect 3feminine singular וַתָּ֫רִץ (Kö i. 352 ; Ba ZMG xliii (1889), 181 thinks Qal ) Judg 9:53 she crushed his skull. Hithpo`el reciprocal, Imperfect 3masculine plural בְּקִרְבָּהּ הַבָּנִים וִיִּתְרֹצְצוּ Gen 25:22 (J) the children crushed (thurst, struck) one another within her.
